title: Illumination-aware Faster R-CNN for Robust Multispectral Pedestrian Detection
authors: Chengyang Li, Dan Song, Ruofeng Tong, Min Tang
architecture type: Cue-driven gating (two-stream detector with illumination-driven gate)
key idea: Small CNN predicts day/night probability from RGB image; learned gate converts it to a weight w for the RGB sub-network and 1-w for the thermal one
results: Illumination-aware weighting beats average weighting by 0.67 points and hard binary switching by 5.03 points
notes: Closest template for our gate, RGB+thermal, weights computed from an explicit reliability cue; we could swap illumination for thermal contrast and valid depth fraction

title: Seeing Through Fog Without Seeing Fog: Deep Multimodal Sensor Fusion in Unseen Adverse Weather
authors: Mario Bijelic, Tobias Gruber, Fahim Mannan, Florian Kraus, Werner Ritter, Klaus Dietmayer, Felix Heide
architecture type: Cue-driven gating (single-shot detector with entropy-steered adaptive fusion)
key idea: Feature fusion between camera, LIDAR, radar, and gated NIR is steered by each sensor's measurement entropy, so degraded sensors contribute less
datasets: Weather driving dataset trained on clear weather only (not public)
results: Generalizes to fog and snow it never saw in training but abstract reports no headline number.
notes: Entropy is a reliable cue computed directly from the image, like thermal contrast; training only on clean data and testing on degraded data mirrors testing on crossover

title: Robust Deep Multi-modal Learning Based on Gated Information Fusion Network
authors: Jaekyum Kim, Junho Koh, Yecheol Kim, Jaehyung Choi, Youngbae Hwang, Jun Won Choi
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (learned spatial gating through per-pixel weight maps)
key idea: Concatenated RGB and LIDAR feature maps & passed them through two 3x3 convolutions + sigmoid to produce one weight map per modality; weighted features are then fused with a 1x1 convolution
results: Beats non-gated baseline in all corrupted input scenarios by up to about 5% AP.
notes: Simples drop-in learned gate; per pixel weights could let the glass region lean on thermal while the background leans on RGB

title: Improving Multispectral Pedestrian Detection by Addressing Modality Imbalance Problems (MBNet)
authors: Kailai Zhou, Linsen Chen, Xun Cao
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (differential modality-aware fusion and illumination-aware feature alignment)
key idea: Fusion module exploits the difference between RGB and thermal features, and an illumination aware module selects and aligns complementary features based on lighting
results: Reports state of the art accuracy and efficient on both datasets (no numbers provided in abstract)
notes: Moves illumination-aware weighting from the output leve (IAF R-CNN) into the features

title: Glass Segmentation with RGB-Thermal Image Pairs
authors: Dong Huo, Jian Wang, Yiming Qian, Yee-Hong Yang
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (dual ResNet-50 encoders & transformer cross-modal fusion & spatial-attention decoder)
key idea: Self-attention computes per-position weights to update RGB and thermal features; the decoder uses spatial attention to weight each modality's encoder features
results: IoU 93.80 vs 88.94 for the RGB-only variant
notes: This is the same dataset we're using, candidate for thermal encoder pretraining or evaluation

title: See, Hear, and Feel: Smart Sensory Fusion for Robotic Manipulation (MULSA)
authors: Hao Li, Yizhi Zhang, Junzhe Zhu, Shaoxiong Wang, Michelle A. Lee, Huazhe Xu, Edward Adelson, Li Fei-Fei, Ruohan Gao, Jiajun Wu
architecture type: Learned gating/ attention (per-modality ResNet-18 & multihead self attention, imitation learned policy
key idea: Vision, audio, and touch encoders feed a self-attention layer across modailities; an MLP predicts actions
results: Dense packing success 1.00 vs 0.60 for concatenation, pouring error 1.41 g vs 2.46 g
notes: Same encoder layout as our Diffusion Policy baseline; standard robotics baseline for smart fusion; attention weights act as implicit reliability

title: Trusted Multi-View Classification
authors: Zongbo Han, Changqing Zhang, Huazhu Fu, Joey Tianyi Zhou
architecture type: Uncertainty-based (evidential (Dirichlet) late fusion with Dempster-Shafer combination)
key idea: Each view outputs evidence for a Dirichlet distribution, giving a per-view uncertainty; views are combined with Dempster-Shafer theory so uncertain views count less
datasets: Handwritten, CUB, Caltech101, PIE, Scene15, HMDB
results: Stays robust when half the views are corrupted with Gaussian noise, where baselines drop significantly
notes: Foundational uncertainty-based fusion modelbut built mailny for classificatoin so adapting to continuous situations like manipulation will require some effort

title: Multimodal Dynamics: Dynamical Fusion for Trustworthy Multimodal Classification
authors: Zongbo Han, Fan Yang, Junzhou Huang, Changqing Zhang, Jianhua Yao
architecture type: Uncertainty-based (2-level dynamic weighting using sparse feature gating and modality confidence)
key idea: Spares gates weight features within each modaility and a confidence head predicts each modality's true class probability
results: Reports better accuracy and trustworthiness than state of the art (no numbers in abstract)
notes: A learned confidence head per modality is a clean design & the sim can supply the supervision (i.e. we know when thermal is at crossover)

title: Provable Dynamic Fusion for Low-Quality Multimodal Data (QMF)
authors: Qingyang Zhang, Haitao Wu, Changqing Zhang, Qinghua Hu, Huazhu Fu, Joey Tianyi Zhou, Xi Peng
key idea: Weight is calculated using an energy-based uncertainty from each modality's logits
datasets: NYU Depth V2, SUN RGB-D, UPMC Food-101, MVSA
results: NYU Depth V2 with noise on 50% of modalities
notes: Includes RGB-D and gives theory for why incertainty-weighted fusion generalizes; code is public

title: MAMMOTH: A Multi-Modal End-to-End Policy for Off-Road Mobility Robust to Missing Modality
authors: Ahaan Kotian, Shivani Subramanyan, Suresh Sundaram
architecture type: Policy-level composition (attention + sparse mixture-of-experts with per-modality routing, diffusion head)
key idea: RGB, thermal, LIDAR, and velocity tokens go through self-attention and a 16-expert MoE with one router per modality; modality dropout in training; a diffusion head outputs trajectories
datasets: Off-road navigation robot in day and night
results: Operates at night where RGB-only baselines can't; daytime goal reaching 33% vs 17% for NoMaD
notes: Closest overall stack to ours (thermal + difusion + modality dropout, but navigation not manipulation); very recent preprint
